topics.concept: Net present value discounts every future cash flow back to today at a chosen rate and subtracts the upfront investment. A positive NPV means the project creates value above the required return; negative means it destroys it. It is the single most trusted rule in capital budgeting because it measures value in dollars, not percentages.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded project cash flow schedules with realistic ramps and one-time costs, discounts at a configurable rate, and reports NPV with a year-by-year present-value table.
topics.name: Net Present Value Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Finance teams screen every capital project with NPV before approving spend.

topics.concept: The internal rate of return is the discount rate that makes NPV exactly zero: the project's implied yield. Solving it needs iteration, typically bisection or Newton steps, because there is no closed form for uneven cash flows. A project clears the hurdle when IRR exceeds the cost of capital, though reinvestment assumptions make it less pure than NPV.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded cash flow series with varied signs and magnitudes, solves IRR by bisection, and compares each project's IRR against a hurdle rate.

key_params.cash_flows: cash flow series with sign changes

topics.name: IRR Solver
topics.real_world_use: Investors quote IRR to compare fund and project performance on a single percentage scale.

topics.concept: Break-even finds the unit volume where total revenue equals total cost: fixed costs divided by contribution margin per unit. Below it the business loses money on every period; above it each extra unit adds margin. Sensitivity around the point shows how fragile the plan is to price or cost slips.
topics.data_idea: Simulates a seeded product with fixed costs, variable cost, and price, computes break-even units and revenue, and charts profit across a volume range.

key_params.fixed_costs: costs that do not vary with volume

topics.name: Break-even Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Founders use break-even analysis to set sales targets a new product must hit to survive.

topics.concept: An amortization schedule splits every loan payment into interest and principal, with early payments mostly interest and later ones mostly principal. The schedule shows total interest paid and how extra principal payments shorten the term. It is the math behind every mortgage statement.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded loan terms with rates and durations, builds the full payment schedule, and quantifies interest saved by extra payments.
topics.name: Loan Amortization Schedule Builder
topics.real_world_use: Lenders and borrowers use amortization schedules to disclose true borrowing costs.

topics.concept: Compounding grows money on both principal and past interest, which is why early saving dominates late saving. A ladder comparison shows the same monthly deposit at different rates and start years side by side. The visual gap between starting at 25 versus 35 is the most persuasive chart in personal finance.
topics.data_idea: Projects seeded contribution schedules at several rates and start ages, compounds monthly, and compares ending balances in a ladder table.
topics.name: Compound Interest Ladder
topics.real_world_use: Advisors use compounding illustrations to motivate retirement saving.

topics.concept: The payback period counts how many years of cash inflow it takes to recover the initial outlay. It ignores the time value of money and everything after payback, which makes it crude but honest about liquidity risk. Discounted payback fixes the first flaw by discounting the inflows.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded project cash flows, computes simple and discounted payback periods, and flags projects that never pay back within the horizon.
topics.name: Payback Period Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Operations managers use payback for quick screening of equipment purchases.

topics.concept: Budget variance analysis compares actuals to plan and splits the gap into price, volume, and mix effects. An unfavorable variance is not automatically bad news: spending more because volume beat plan is success, while spending more at the same volume is waste. The decomposition tells which story the numbers are telling.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded budget versus actual line items with volume and rate drivers, computes variances, and decomposes each into price, volume, and mix components.
topics.name: Budget Variance Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams present variance bridges in monthly business reviews to explain performance.

topics.concept: Runway analysis projects when cash hits zero given current burn and expected revenue. It separates fixed burn from variable spend so leaders see which cuts actually extend life. Scenario toggles, like a hiring freeze or a price increase, turn the model into a decision tool instead of a countdown.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded monthly cash flows with hiring plans and revenue ramps, computes runway under base and scenario cases, and charts the cash-zero crossing.
topics.name: Cash Runway Projector
topics.real_world_use: Startup operators rerun runway models before every board meeting and hiring decision.

topics.concept: Depreciation spreads an asset's cost over its useful life, and the method changes reported profit: straight-line is even, declining-balance front-loads expense, and units-of-production ties cost to usage. The choice affects taxes and ratios without moving a dollar of cash. Modeling all three side by side makes the trade-off concrete.
topics.data_idea: Creates a seeded fixed-asset register with costs and lives, applies straight-line, declining-balance, and units-of-production methods, and compares annual expense and book value.

key_params.assets: assets with cost and useful life
key_params.salvage_value: residual value at end of life

topics.name: Depreciation Schedule Comparator
topics.real_world_use: Controllers choose depreciation methods to manage reported earnings and tax timing.

topics.concept: A margin ladder stacks gross, operating, and net margin for a business or product line, showing where each layer of cost bites. Expanding the ladder over time reveals whether scale is improving profitability or just growing revenue. Benchmarking the ladder against peers exposes structural advantages or bloated cost layers.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded income-statement lines across periods, computes each margin layer, and benchmarks the ladder against a peer distribution.

key_params.cost_layers: COGS, operating, and other cost layers

topics.name: Profit Margin Ladder
topics.real_world_use: Equity analysts dissect margin ladders to judge whether growth is profitable.

topics.concept: A discounted cash flow model projects free cash flow for several years, discounts each year at the weighted average cost of capital, and adds a terminal value for everything beyond the forecast. The terminal value often dominates, which is why growth and discount assumptions deserve the most scrutiny. Done well, DCF anchors valuation in fundamentals instead of market mood.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded company with revenue growth, margins, and capex assumptions, projects five years of free cash flow, discounts at WACC, and adds a Gordon-growth terminal value.
topics.name: DCF Valuation Model
topics.real_world_use: Investment bankers and corporate development teams anchor acquisition bids with DCF valuations.

topics.concept: Revenue never lands exactly on plan, so a Monte Carlo model draws thousands of possible futures from distributions for price, volume, and churn. The result is a probability distribution of revenue, not a single number, with percentiles a planner can actually commit to. It replaces false precision with honest ranges.
topics.data_idea: Samples seeded distributions for units, price, and churn across thousands of trials, aggregates annual revenue outcomes, and reports the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles.
topics.name: Monte Carlo Revenue Simulator
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams use revenue simulations to set ranges for guidance instead of single-point forecasts.

topics.concept: The weighted average cost of capital blends the cost of equity, from the capital asset pricing model, with the after-tax cost of debt, weighted by market values. It is the hurdle rate for new investments and the discount rate in DCF models. Small errors in beta or the market risk premium swing valuations more than most realize.
topics.data_idea: Computes seeded cost-of-equity inputs, debt costs, and capital weights, derives WACC, and shows valuation sensitivity to beta and risk premium shifts.

key_params.debt_ratio: share of debt in capital structure

topics.name: WACC Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Corporate finance teams refresh WACC annually to keep hurdle rates current.

topics.concept: A three-statement model links the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement so every change flows through consistently: revenue drives receivables, capex drives depreciation, and net income feeds retained earnings. Balancing the balance sheet is the integrity check that everything ties. It is the minimum viable model for planning a company's finances.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded base-year financial position, projects three linked statements over five years with working-capital drivers, and validates that the balance sheet balances.
topics.name: Three Statement Model Lite
topics.real_world_use: Analysts build three-statement models as the foundation for budgeting and valuation.

topics.concept: Scenario modeling reruns the same financial model under base, upside, and downside assumptions to bound the outcome range. The discipline is keeping scenarios internally consistent: a downside case cannot assume strong pricing and weak volume at once. Comparing scenario outputs shows which decisions are robust and which bet everything on one future.
topics.data_idea: Takes a seeded base model and perturbs growth, margin, and capex drivers per scenario, then compares NPV, cash trough, and funding need across scenarios.
topics.name: Scenario Model Comparator
topics.real_world_use: Boards review scenario packs to approve plans that survive the downside, not just the base case.

topics.concept: Unit economics reduce a business to the profit of one unit: one customer, one order, one subscriber. Contribution margin per unit, payback time, and the LTV to CAC ratio all derive from this single view. If the unit economics do not work, scaling only multiplies the loss.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded per-unit P&L with acquisition cost, revenue, and variable cost, computes contribution margin, payback, and ratio metrics with segment splits.
topics.name: Unit Economics Model
topics.real_world_use: Investors demand unit economics before funding a company to scale.

topics.concept: Buying equipment is capex: capitalized and depreciated, hitting cash now and profit later. Renting or subscribing is opex: expensed immediately, hitting profit now. The comparison must be done in present-value terms over the full horizon, including maintenance, tax shields, and residual value, or the cheaper-looking option wins unfairly.
topics.data_idea: Models a seeded asset need under buy, lease, and subscribe options with cash flows, tax shields, and residuals, then compares total present cost.
topics.name: CapEx versus OpEx Comparator
topics.real_world_use: IT and operations leaders use buy-versus-rent analysis for infrastructure decisions.

topics.concept: The cash conversion cycle measures days from paying suppliers to collecting from customers: inventory days plus receivable days minus payable days. A shorter cycle means less cash trapped in working capital. Improving any leg, like collecting faster or holding less stock, frees cash without raising a dollar of funding.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded inventory, receivable, and payable balances with sales and COGS, computes DIO, DSO, DPO, and the cycle trend with improvement scenarios.

key_params.cogs: cost of goods sold per period

topics.name: Cash Conversion Cycle Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Treasury teams track the cycle to minimize external financing needs.

topics.concept: A tornado chart ranks model inputs by how much the output swings when each input moves from low to high. The widest bars sit on top, instantly showing which assumptions deserve diligence. It turns a hundred-line model into a prioritized list of what actually matters.
topics.data_idea: Runs a seeded DCF or budget model while sweeping each input across its range one at a time, ranks inputs by output swing, and renders the tornado chart.
topics.name: Sensitivity Tornado Chart
topics.real_world_use: Analysts attach tornado charts to investment memos to show which assumptions carry the thesis.

topics.concept: The Gordon growth version of the dividend discount model values a share as next year's dividend divided by the required return minus perpetual growth. It only fits mature, dividend-paying companies where growth is stable and below the discount rate. Its beauty is transparency: every assumption sits in the open.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded dividend histories with growth estimates, applies the Gordon formula across required-return scenarios, and flags cases where growth exceeds the discount rate.
topics.name: Dividend Discount Model
topics.real_world_use: Value investors use dividend models to sanity-check prices of mature dividend payers.

topics.concept: A leveraged buyout model layers debt onto an acquisition: a debt schedule with mandatory and optional repayments, interest that reduces taxes, and an exit sale that repays the rest. Returns come from deleveraging, growth, and multiple expansion, and the model shows how much leverage the cash flows can actually support. It is the core engine of private equity underwriting.
topics.data_idea: Creates a seeded target company with cash flows, structures tranches of debt with terms, runs the debt schedule to exit, and computes levered IRR and money-on-invested-capital.
topics.name: Leveraged Buyout Model Lite
topics.real_world_use: Private equity associates build LBO models to set maximum bid prices for targets.

topics.concept: Real options value managerial flexibility, like the right to expand, delay, or abandon a project, using option-pricing logic instead of static NPV. A project with negative NPV can still be worth starting if it buys a cheap option on a big upside. Binomial lattices make the intuition computable without heavy math.
topics.data_idea: Models a seeded staged investment as a binomial lattice of future values, values the expand and abandon options at each node, and compares option value to static NPV.
topics.name: Real Options Valuator Lite
topics.real_world_use: Energy and pharma firms value staged R&D and exploration rights with real options.

topics.concept: A rolling forecast drops the oldest month and adds a new one every cycle, so the plan always looks twelve or eighteen months ahead. It adapts to reality instead of freezing a budget made last fall. The engine part is automating driver-based updates so reforecasting takes days, not weeks.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded actuals with trend and seasonality, regenerates the rolling forecast each month from driver models, and tracks forecast accuracy over the roll.
topics.name: Rolling Forecast Engine
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams run rolling forecasts to keep plans current without annual budget theater.

topics.concept: A merger is accretive when the combined earnings per share rise after the deal and dilutive when they fall. The model combines the two income statements, adds synergies, subtracts financing costs and new shares, and compares pro-forma EPS to standalone EPS. Accretion math decides whether a deal creates or destroys shareholder value on paper.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded acquirer and target financials, applies purchase price, financing mix, and synergy assumptions, then computes accretion or dilution with sensitivity to the price paid.
topics.name: Merger Accretion Dilution Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Corporate development teams run accretion analysis before recommending acquisitions to the board.

topics.concept: Foreign-exchange exposure measures how much profit moves when currencies shift: translation exposure on reported results and transaction exposure on actual cash flows. Hedging with forwards locks rates but costs money, so the model compares hedged versus unhedged outcomes across rate scenarios. The goal is not to predict currencies but to bound the damage.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded multi-currency revenues and costs, simulates exchange-rate paths, and compares unhedged, partially hedged, and fully hedged profit distributions.
topics.name: FX Exposure Model
topics.real_world_use: Multinational treasuries size hedge programs from exposure models like this.

topics.concept: The economic order quantity balances ordering costs against holding costs: order too often and setup costs pile up, order too much and capital sits on shelves. The square-root formula finds the quantity that minimizes total cost. Safety stock then covers demand variability during lead time.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded demand with variability and lead times, computes EOQ and reorder points per SKU, and compares total inventory cost against naive ordering rules.

key_params.holding_cost: cost to hold one unit a year

topics.name: EOQ Inventory Cost Optimizer
topics.real_world_use: Supply chain planners set order policies from EOQ math to minimize working capital.

topics.concept: Working capital forecasting projects receivables, payables, and inventory from revenue and cost drivers, because growth consumes cash before it generates it. A company can be profitable and still run dry if working capital balloons. Linking each balance to its driver turns the forecast into an early warning for cash crunches.
topics.data_idea: Projects seeded revenue and COGS with driver-linked DSO, DPO, and DIO, forecasts the working-capital need by month, and flags periods where funding gaps appear.
topics.name: Working Capital Forecaster
topics.real_world_use: CFOs of growing companies forecast working capital to size credit lines before they are needed.

topics.concept: A deterministic DCF gives one value; a Monte Carlo DCF gives a distribution by sampling growth rates, margins, and the discount rate. The output shows the probability the investment clears its hurdle instead of a single fragile number. It forces the analyst to state uncertainty explicitly rather than hiding it in a point estimate.
topics.data_idea: Samples seeded assumption distributions, values the company thousands of times, and reports the valuation distribution with the probability of exceeding the asking price.

key_params.assumption_distributions: ranges for growth, margin, and WACC

topics.name: Monte Carlo DCF Valuator
topics.real_world_use: Buy-side analysts present valuation ranges from stochastic DCFs to investment committees.

topics.concept: Zero-based budgeting starts every line item at zero and requires each dollar to be justified, instead of last year plus a percent. It is expensive in effort but exposes legacy spending nobody would approve fresh. The tool structures the justification workflow: decision packages, rankings, and cutoff lines.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded prior-year budget with decision packages, ranks them by value score, and applies a funding cutoff to produce the zero-based plan.

key_params.decision_packages: spend proposals with costs and benefits

topics.name: Zero-Based Budgeting Tool
topics.real_world_use: Companies under margin pressure use zero-based budgeting to reset cost bases.

topics.concept: Activity-based costing traces overhead to products through the activities that actually consume resources: setups, inspections, shipments. Traditional allocation by labor hours misprices complex low-volume products. ABC reveals the true cost of variety so pricing and mix decisions rest on facts.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded factory with activities, cost pools, and product consumption rates, allocates overhead by driver, and compares ABC unit costs to traditional allocation.
topics.name: Activity-Based Cost Allocator
topics.real_world_use: Manufacturers use ABC to price custom and low-volume products profitably.
